Confirmed: the finding is valid. I ran Jest 29.7.0 with `testFailureExitCode: 200`; it completed normally and exited 200. The current guard incorrectly classifies that as an incomplete run. Jest explicitly supports configurable failure codes. [Documentation](https://jestjs.io/docs/configuration#testfailureexitcode-number)

This predates our last commit. Simply removing the guard could allow crashed runs to report PASS again. The fix needs explicit knowledge of the configured failure code, while retaining conservative handling of ambiguous statuses.

The finding remains open; I haven’t changed the code.
